customer_question: Our existing registration already includes HOGP. Do we need to test or register anything else for this new product, and is it true that BAS/DIS/HIDS are now also mandatory?
question_variants: Does HOGP registration now require BAS, DIS, and HIDS as well?
We already have HOGP -- why are BAS/DIS/HIDS items being tested too?
If the BAS/DIS/HIDS items don't pass this round, can we still register?
Is this minimum testing required, or can we register without passing it?
actual_issue: A keyboard manufacturer's existing registration already covered HOGP, but under the current registration system, registering a product with the HOGP-Device role now also mandates testing the minimum required items of BAS, DIS, and HIDS as a cascading dependency, which the customer had not anticipated and needed to be informed was not optional for completing the registration.
plain_english_explanation: A keyboard's Bluetooth profile (HOGP) used to be the only thing that needed testing for this kind of product. Under a more recent set of rules, choosing that profile automatically pulls in three other related profiles that must also pass at least their minimum required tests, even if the customer's existing registration never needed them before. If those required tests aren't passed, the registration simply can't be completed -- there's no way to register while skipping them.
consultant_answer: The customer's existing registration (Input Devices/End Product, v5.0) already includes HOGP, and its existing ICS was provided as a starting point, with a request for the customer to flag any changes or additions needed (e.g., a specific item flipping from not-supported to supported). However, under the current registration site, the HOGP-Device role now cascades mandatory testing of BAS, DIS, and HIDS as well -- at minimum, each profile's required items will be tested. If the customer wants to register support for functionality beyond each profile's bare minimum required items, the corresponding additional ICS items need to be specified. When asked whether this round's test items could be skipped if they returned Fail or Indecisive, the answer was direct: this round's test items are the minimum required for registration, and the certification cannot be registered unless the items that came back Fail or Indecisive are passed.
decision_logic: Selecting the HOGP-Device role in the current registration system mandatorily cascades minimum-item testing requirements for BAS, DIS, and HIDS, regardless of whether a prior registration for the same or a similar product predates this requirement; passing these minimum items (or applying an accepted alternative such as referencing an existing third-party registration that already covers them) is a precondition for completing the registration, not an optional enhancement.
final_recommendation: When scoping a new HOGP-Device role registration, inform the customer upfront that BAS, DIS, and HIDS minimum-item testing is now a mandatory cascading requirement, request the existing ICS as a baseline along with any deltas, and make clear that any resulting Fail/Indecisive items on these now-mandatory profiles must be resolved before registration can proceed.
risk_if_done_wrong: Assuming the product's prior HOGP-only registration scope still applies, or that newly-mandatory BAS/DIS/HIDS minimum items can be skipped, would block the registration from being completed once the Fail/Indecisive results are reached.
